headToHead.structure: Reactions. Take Me Out: lights go off in waves, and Paddy chats with only a few women about why. Dating Game/Blind Date: the chooser listens and saves judgement; 'Our Graham' recaps before the pick. Ours: the star delivers a line and a visible mark after every single answer, nine times an episode, in a fixed slot. The rhythm is a metronome and the line pool cannot keep up, which is why so many reactions answer the persona rather than the sentence. Bar.
headToHead.pick: Love Island recoupling holds the name to the last word, with qualities first. Ours puts the name first in every pick line ('Quill, lift the helmet...', 'Crumb. Chrome, opinions...', 'Miss Tilly. The key.', 'Tilly. Picked.'), so the six-second hold is spent and the first syllable after it settles every bet. Bar.

voiceSeparation: Pixel is identifiable blind (fragments, mid-sentence drops, scores, clip/skip). Maximilian mostly (short declaratives, Madam/Mr, removal of guests), though his reactions drift into pure prop gags. Vesper is the weak one: her rhythm ('X, and Y, and Z') is recognisable but her content is radio set dressing (trucker, baker, night nurse, kettle, gritter) rather than a stance. Her two CAST tics barely appear: she dedicates a song as an insult once in four episodes, and she never lets a silence do the work outside the scripted hold. Her real recurring move is 'I'm old', which hybrid-02/ep-02 runs six times.

pickMakesSense: Mostly follows standings, but the visible marks lie to bettors. Vesper charmed Prince twice then cut him (script-r1/ep-06); Maximilian charmed Nav then cut him with a threat (ep-02); Pixel picked Quill after cringing at him in round two (ep-04); Vesper picked Quill with 0 charmed, 3 unsure (hybrid-02/ep-02). Hidden cards explain some of it at the reveal, but the mark a viewer bets on is often the opposite of what the star then does, and the pick line itself never says why.
biggestGap: Star reactions are chosen by who spoke and which card the line hit, not by what the line said: about a third of them answer a tic the suitor never used this episode (recalculating, variant A, shipping it, clause four, escalate, please, the chart) or the avatar (visor, crown, flip-flops, moth), and charmed is handed out on tag hits regardless of quality (47 percent of all marks). The bar's undercut always seizes a word from the sentence just said, so the fix is to make every reaction hook a specific noun or phrase from the preceding line (authored answer and reaction written as pairs in scripted mode, the model given that word as a hard requirement in live mode) and to award charmed only to the night's best one or two lines.
structuralChange: Name the winner last. Today the six-second hold is followed by a pick line that opens with the winner's name, so the climax is spent on the first syllable. Change the pick to: hold (6 s, silent), then the star speaks one recap clause per finalist, each quoting that finalist's best moment of the night in the star's voice (about 4 s each, order randomised so the first clause is not a tell), a 2-second silence with both finalists lit, then the name alone as the final word, then the winner's line. This is the Love Island recouple and Blind Date's 'Our Graham' recap fused, it gives the last betting window a real payoff, and it forces the star to call back something actually said.
structuralChangeAlt: Second option if time allows: in rounds one and two the star speaks a reaction to only the best and worst answer; the other answers get the mark alone, like Take Me Out's lights with Paddy chatting to a few. Halves the reactions the bank must feed and makes each spoken one rarer.
